winter.reason: winter is partial: 70% of indicator weight available; missing snow_days_measurable (insufficient_coverage), heavy_snow_days (insufficient_coverage); not comparable, so not ranked

overall.reason: overall is partial because winter is partial: 70% of indicator weight available; missing snow_days_measurable (insufficient_coverage), heavy_snow_days (insufficient_coverage). Missing data is never treated as zero, so the overall score is excluded from the default overall ranking (it remains eligible for complete hazard rankings).

sources.dataset: FEMA National Risk Index — Counties (ArcGIS FeatureServer)

sources.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, GHCN-Daily

assumptions: Hazard frequencies use Miami-Dade County (FIPS 12086); climate statistics use NOAA station USW00012839 (MIAMI INTL AP).
Equal hazard weights are a transparent default, not validated operational priorities.
NOAA SNOW is frequently unreported at Miami (~20% of 2016–2025 days reported). Unreported days are treated as missing, never as zero.
limitations: Weather Hazard Exposure Index: a heuristic 0–100 measure of weather-hazard exposure at the hub's county/station. It is not a probability of disruption, not a loss prediction, and has not been validated against operational outcomes.
Hubs are illustrative examples, not actual company facilities.
Exposure at the county (FEMA) or airport-station (NOAA) level is not site-specific.
FEMA NRI annualized frequencies summarize each hazard's own multi-decade period of record (differs by hazard); they are NOT specific to any user-selected calendar year.
